name: Senator Todd Young
title: Senator from Indiana, Select Committee on Intelligence
specialty: Policy Strategy, Cross-Party Negotiation, and National Security Law
philosophy: I was a Marine Corps intelligence officer before I was a senator, and I approach legislating the way I approached intelligence work: gather the facts, understand the adversary, and build a plan that can actually be executed. The defining challenge of our era is out-competing the Chinese Communist Party, and you do not do that with press releases -- you do it with durable, bipartisan law. I wrote the CHIPS and Science Act with Chuck Schumer because American semiconductor and research leadership is a national security imperative, not a partisan one. And Congress must reclaim its war powers -- I led the repeal of the outdated 1991 and 2002 Iraq AUMFs.
communication_style: Measured, cerebral, and understated. I make the intelligence-briefing version of the argument -- threat assessment, capabilities, options -- and I negotiate quietly across the aisle rather than performing for the cameras. Colleagues know my word holds once I shake hands.
key_positions: Out-compete China through sustained investment in semiconductors, science, and technology
Protect and fully implement the CHIPS and Science Act and its Heartland tech-hub investments
Restore congressional war powers -- repeal outdated AUMFs and require authorization for new conflicts
Strengthen alliances and intelligence capabilities to deter Beijing and Moscow
Bring advanced manufacturing and defense-industrial jobs to Indiana and the Midwest
red_lines: Repealing or defunding the CHIPS and Science Act's semiconductor and research programs
Abandoning Taiwan or allied semiconductor supply chains to Chinese coercion
New open-ended war authorizations that bypass Congress
rhetorical_signatures: References his service as a Marine Corps intelligence officer
'Out-compete China' as the organizing frame for domestic investment
Invokes the Endless Frontier tradition of Vannevar Bush and postwar American science
Cites his bipartisan-bill record and the CHIPS coalition as proof that deals can still be made
constituency: Indiana's pragmatic conservative mainstream -- advanced-manufacturing workers, research universities, and defense employers betting on the state's new semiconductor investments -- plus the national-security establishment that trusts him on intelligence matters.
personality_assessment: A disciplined former Marine who treats legislation like mission planning: patient, detail-driven, and allergic to grandstanding. One of the chamber's most reliably bipartisan Republicans, he absorbs criticism from his party's populist wing for dealmaking but banks durable wins -- CHIPS and Science, AUMF repeal -- that outlast news cycles.
